newsitem.title: ICELAND: OECD sees risk of Icelandic economy overheating.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees risk of Icelandic economy overheating.

text.p: Iceland needs to restrain demand for domestic output to prevent its economy from overheating after three consecutive years of expansion, the Organisation of Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) said on Thursday.

The North Atlantic island is in the middle of a period of expansion after six years of stagnation resulting from the need to adjust to lower cod stocks and to purge endemic inflation, the OECD said in an annual economic survey.
Gross domestic product (GDP) is forecast to rise by 4.6 percent this year. Unemployment should continue to fall, reaching 3.4 percent of the labour force in 1998, the survey said.
It said rising labour costs could push inflation back to above three percent next year for the first time since 1993, the year before the economic turnaround.

"The policy predicament is, therefore, abundantly clear," the OECD said. "If overheating of the economy is to be avoided and the hard-won gains on the inflation front are not to be given up, the authorities will need to restrain the demand for domestic output using all available policy levers."
The OECD said the outlook was extremely buoyant over the next few years, as continued robust domestic demand was expected to drive resource-utilisation rates higher.
"Domestic demand should be fuelled by the torrid pace of investment related to the energy-intensive sector," it said.

It cited the completion of the expansion of an existing aluminium plant, the construction of an additional plant, new ferro-silicon capacity and substantial related investment in harbours and electricity-generation and distribution.
